Amazon.com (NasdaqGS:AMZN) faces a potential criminal trial in Italy over alleged unpaid import VAT and customs duties on non EU goods.

Italian prosecutors are targeting Amazon's European unit and managers over marketplace sales of millions of products imported from outside the EU.

The case centers on alleged failures to account for VAT and duties on third party cross border shipments handled through Amazon's European marketplace.

The Italian investigation into alleged unpaid import VAT and customs duties on Amazon's marketplace activity reshapes the broader risk picture investors are tracking. Check out 5 other big wins that Amazon.com investors should know about.

For a wider view on how legal and regulatory scrutiny can affect pricing power and quality across the sector, compare this with 35 high quality undervalued stocks.

NasdaqGS:AMZN 1-Year Stock Price Chart

Amazon.com runs a global online and physical retail network, including a large European marketplace where third party merchants ship cross border goods that rely heavily on local tax and customs frameworks. The Italian probe hits a part of the operation that connects non EU sellers to EU based shoppers rather than its US focused retail or subscription services.

See how Amazon.com's balance sheet measures up.

Italian VAT case stresses Amazon.com's execution risk on compliance, not its AI engine

The potential Italian trial puts a spotlight on Amazon.com's ability to police its own marketplace logistics and tax processes, which leans into the Narrative risk around rising regulatory scrutiny on how the group operates. It does not directly hit the AI and AWS centered catalyst that depends on very large CapEx turning into long duration contracts. However, it reminds you that complex global structures can attract legal challenges that add cost and management bandwidth drain. For the bull case that leans on high quality earnings from AWS, advertising and new platforms like Amazon Leo, this development mostly clips the "clean execution" side of the story rather than the demand side.

See how these catalysts shape Amazon.com's path to a $331 fair value.

The practical checkpoint is when Italian authorities decide whether to send Amazon's European unit and managers to trial and, if they do, the first detailed disclosures of any proposed settlement amounts or court findings on VAT and duties, which would set clearer boundaries around potential fines and ongoing compliance obligations.

title: Generac: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Generac: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 3:05 PM MST 3 min read
GNRC
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Generac (NYSE:GNRC) announced record quarterly net sales of $1.29 billion, powered by growth in its data center backup generator business. Rapid expansion in commercial power infrastructure gives the company a multiyear revenue runway as technology operators expand artificial intelligence computing capacity.

Three things management said stand out.

1. Data Center Generator Backlog Tripled to $4.5 Billion Following an Amazon Supply Deal

Hyperscale cloud providers are locking in backup power supply years in advance to protect massive infrastructure investments. Generac secured a multiyear supply deal with Amazon, expanding its overall data center order pipeline.

Initial deliveries in this agreement are expected to be a combined $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028, driving the increase in our backlog for products sold to the data center market to approximately $4.5 billion nearly tripling from just 90 days ago.
-- Aaron Jagdfeld, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Manufacturing Capacity Is Tripling Without Heavy Capital Expenditure Requirements

Scaling large megawatt generator manufacturing usually requires heavy fixed-asset spending that weighs on returns. Management is expanding output through existing facilities and added assembly lines, keeping capital requirements modest relative to expected revenue.

The relatively small incremental investment needed to ramp capacity further highlights the capital light nature of our business and the incredibly strong ROI that we expect to realize from these investments.
-- Aaron Jagdfeld, President and Chief Executive Officer

3. Portable Generator Market Leadership Drives Standby System Upgrades

Entry-level portable generators serve as a direct customer acquisition funnel for higher-margin home standby units. Reclaiming top market share in portable generators feeds the long-term residential upgrade pipeline.

Importantly, our customer demographic data shows that more than 50% of the purchasers of home standby generators either previously or currently owned a portable generator. Making the trade up experience from a portable to a standby product an important 1 for our residential business.
-- Aaron Jagdfeld, President and Chief Executive Officer

Looking Ahead

Demand for artificial intelligence power backup is accelerating across global markets. Generac maintains structural advantages in customized packaging integration and short lead times, while management monitors factory staffing ramps and supply chain execution.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG, NASDAQ:GOOGL) both reported third-quarter results in late October. Both now face a valuation event outside their own businesses, because Anthropic expects to price its IPO on November 18 and begin trading on Nasdaq as ANT on November 19.

24/7 Wall St.

A Reuters calculation puts their combined stakes at $411 billion if shares price at $78, the top of the $70 to $78 range. That windfall measures total stake value at the IPO price rather than profit, and neither company has commented on it. Amazon holds the larger and cheaper position, although much of it arrives only over time.

Amazon's Stake Carries More Weight in Its Stock Price

At $78, Amazon's position is worth $271.8 billion against $18.0 billion invested. Google's is worth $139 billion against $33.3 billion, and that value includes about $10.0 billion Google is spending in the IPO placement itself.

Amazon's stake equals about 9.3% of its market value at Tuesday's close, compared with about 3.9% for Alphabet. Because of that gap, the IPO price changes the sum-of-the-parts case for Amazon far more than for Alphabet.

title: Amazon and Microsoft Lead the Cloud Market. One of Them Has Far Greater Upside.
detail:
Amazon and Microsoft Lead the Cloud Market. One of Them Has Far Greater Upside.
Geoffrey Seiler, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 12:05 PM MST 5 min read
AMZN
MSFT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Following the midterm elections and sweeping victories by candidates opposed to artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, there has been a lot of debate about which AI companies are best positioned in this new political climate.

However, the general consensus seems to be that leading cloud computing companies with strong businesses, like Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), are well positioned to benefit. Of these two, I think Amazon has a lot more upside. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Cloud leaders

Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft's Azure are the two largest cloud providers. With the rise of AI, both companies have seen their cloud computing businesses take off.

Microsoft has recorded 13 straight quarters of 30% or more Azure growth, with a 48% increase last quarter to $33.2 billion. AWS has seen its growth accelerate to its fastest level in nearly five years, climbing 39% to $46 billion last quarter.

Microsoft's cloud business continues to be bolstered by its relationship with OpenAI. The company has priority access to OpenAI's models and products through 2032, and it owns a 27% stake in the maker of large language models. Microsoft also has huge commitments from OpenAI, which is a big reason for its huge $677 billion backlog.

Amazon also has a huge backlog, which more than doubled last quarter to $578 billion. The company has a close relationship with and a large stake in Anthropic, which has committed to spending over $100 billion with AWS. It also has a partnership with OpenAI around agentic AI. Amazon offers access to various third-party AI models through its Bedrock solution, which has helped drive growth.

What sets Amazon apart from Microsoft, though, is its custom chip business. Earlier this year, Amazon said its custom chips business -- which included its Trainium AI accelerator and Graviton custom ARM Holdings-based central processing unit (CPU) -- was a $20 billion run-rate business, or roughly $50 billion when including internal use.

Last quarter, it said its chip business more than doubled and that chip commitments have soared 20-fold. Demand is so high for its chips that it plans to start selling them to external data centers late next year. Amazon's custom chip business is both a revenue driver and a cost saving, helping it reduce inference costs and giving it better returns than with graphics processing units (GPUs).

Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN) shares moved lower 1.64% to $269.29 at 10.35 a.m. ET on Wednesday, November 11, in regular trading, after Anthropic's amended filing set out how Amazon Web Services' convertible notes turn into Class N shares when the IPO closes. Up to 276,827,518 shares go to AWS, subject to an ownership cap.

AMZN GF Value chart

At the $74 midpoint of Anthropic's range, those conversion shares alone would be worth about $20.5 billion. TradingKey's read of the filing puts Amazon's total holding at roughly 1.92 billion Class N shares, about $142.1 billion at the midpoint. Those shares carry economic rights but no general voting power, and Anthropic runs workloads on AWS Trainium chips.

A $142 billion stake would equal about 4.8% of Amazon's $2.96 trillion market value, making Anthropic's post-IPO price a visible swing factor for Amazon's non-operating income. The bigger lever is AWS: every Claude workload on Trainium supports Amazon's custom-chip economics, though Anthropic also spreads compute across Google, NVIDIA and AMD. GuruFocus gives Amazon a GF Score of 94/100, with Profitability Rank 8/10, Momentum Rank 8/10, Financial Strength 7/10 and GF Value Rank 7/10. At $269.29, the shares trade 4.0% above GuruFocus's GF Value of $258.98, which GuruFocus labels "Fairly Valued." Anthropic's final IPO price sets the first public mark.
